{{Quote|We will require the egg. Bring us the egg.|translated=1|Chettkap|<ref name="Mandalorian2" />}}
'''Mudhorn eggs''' were large, [[Hair|fur-covered]] [[egg]]s laid by the [[Sentience|non-sentient]] [[mudhorn]] [[species]]. They were called "sooga" in [[Jawaese]] and the [[Jawa]]s loved to eat the yolk of such eggs.

==Description==
{{Quote|What is it with Jawas and mudhorn eggs? If they're making omelettes, they better make enough for all of us!|Sentinel|<ref name="Hunters">''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]''</ref>}}
The mudhorn egg<ref name="HasLab">{{SW|url=news/haslab-hasbro-razor-crest-interview|text=If the HasLab ''Razor Crest'' is the Bounty, We're All on the Hunt}}</ref> was a type of large [[egg]], covered in [[Color|brown]] [[Hair|fur]] similar to in appearance and texture to a mudhorn's hide. Being oviparous, Mudhorns would lay only a single egg per clutch, burying them within the muddy [[cave]]-nests found across the surface of [[planet]] [[Arvala-7]]. Filled with a thick yellow-orange yolk, these eggs were considered a delicacy by [[Jawa]]s, who consumed their yolk raw by the handful, though they proved difficult to acquire without outside assistance due to the scarcity and ferocity of mudhorn [[Parent|mothers]].<ref name="Mandalorian2" />

==History==
{{Quote|The Egg! The Egg! The Egg! The Egg!|translated=1|Chettkap's tribe|<ref name="Mandalorian2" />}}
[[File:Mudhorn-eggnog.jpg|left|200px|thumb|A glass of Mudhorn Eggnog]]
In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> a [[bounty hunter]] known as [[Din Djarin]] sought an egg from a [[mudhorn cave]] at the request of an Offworld Jawa [[Chettkap's tribe|tribe]] led by [[chief]] [[Chettkap]], in exchange for parts the tribe had stolen from the bounty hunter's [[gunship]], the ''[[Razor Crest]]''.<ref name="Mandalorian2" /> That same year,<ref name="Hunters Date">{{HuntersDate}}</ref> the Jawa [[Hunter (Grand Arena)|Hunter]] team [[Utooni]] accessorized a mudhorn egg as part of one of their many costumes in the [[Grand Arena]].<ref name="Hunters" />

At some point the [[Artiodac]] [[chef]] [[Strono Tuggs]] acquired a mudhorn egg from some Jawas on Arvala-7 while trying to purchase a [[hypersonic oven]] and was able to create a batch of Mudhorn Eggnog that lasted him an entire season. He later included a recipe for the beverage in his second cookbook, ''[[The Life Day Cookbook]]'', which he released at some point after publishing his first [[The Official Black Spire Outpost Cookbook|cookbook]]<ref name="LDCookbook" /> in [[34 ABY]].<ref name="Date">{{BSOCookbookDate}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Utooni-Mudhorn-Egg-Sticker.png|right|200px|thumb|A mundhorn egg sticker in ''Star Wars: Hunters'']]
Mudhorn eggs first appeared in [[Chapter 2: The Child|Chapter 2]] of [[Jon Favreau]]'s [[2019]] [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', directed by [[Rick Famuyiwa]],<ref name="Mandalorian2" /> which aired on [[November 15]], 2019.<ref name="DTCI">{{WebCite|url=https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/documents/the_mandalorian_project_one-sheet_10_ec1e005f.pdf|text=The Mandalorian Media Kit|work=[https://dtcimedia.disney.com Disney Direct-to-Consumer & International]|archivedate=20230315011507}}</ref>

According to the ''[[Star Wars: The Life Day Cookbook]]'', written by [[Jenn Fujikawa]] and [[Marc Sumerak]]<ref name="LDCookbook" /> and released on [[November 2]], [[2021]],<ref name="Preview">{{SW|url=news/the-life-day-cookbook-exclusive-preview|text=Prepare a Feast Fit for a Wookiee With ''The Life Day Cookbook'' - Exclusive Preview}}</ref> the [[In-universe|out-of-universe]] recipe requires [[Wikipedia:Milk|whole milk]], [[Wikipedia:Half and half|half-and-half]], [[Wikipedia:Vanilla extract|vanilla extract]], a [[Wikipedia:Cinnamon|cinnamon stick]], [[Wikipedia:Salt|salt]], [[Wikipedia:Yolk|egg yolks]], [[Wikipedia:White sugar|granulated sugar]], [[Wikipedia:Egg white|egg whites]], [[Wikipedia:Powdered sugar|confectioners' sugar]], [[Wikipedia:Nutmeg|ground nutmeg]], and ground cinnamon.<ref name="LDCookbook" />
